brief: The weather is the last system in this town still driven by a variable that stopped varying. `stepClouds()` decides every front with `const heavy = day >= 1 && R() < 0.3 + 0.24 * richness()`, the rain roll beneath it scales on `(0.6 + rich)`, and `richness()` is `clamp(day/16, 0, 1)` — pinned at 1 since real minute fifteen. Six other systems now read `season()`; this one reads a dead ramp. Put the fronts on the year: a winter of overcast that arrives more often, sits lower and lasts longer, against summer skies mostly clear and breaking into rarer, heavier showers. `frontLeft = 24 + R()*36` is the front cadence and is flat too. Anchor at `SEASON_START` exactly as #14, #17, #18 and #19 did, so day one is provably the town as it was.
successLooksLike: A pinned January afternoon and a pinned July afternoon on the same seed are obviously different skies — one a low grey lid, one blue with a bank standing off — and a folded multi-year probe reports more overcast hours in winter and fewer but heavier showers in summer, with the annual rain total within reach of HEAD's.
avoid: Do not add snow, fog, or a new precipitation type: this is the year arriving in a system that already exists, not a new system. Do not raise the total amount of rain — a diorama that is wet more of the time is worse to look at and the census cannot see the difference. Two things are folded in and both are part of the same seam, not extras. (1) c8: the rain roll is gated on `daylight > 0.15`, so a front peaking overnight builds full cover and can never rain — in an 11.5-hour winter day that is most of the clock, and it would make the season you have just made cloudiest the one least able to rain. `weatherComing()` also damps on daylight, for a different and still-correct reason (the town must not stand under umbrellas at midnight); do not conflate them. The question here is whether rain may START in the dark, not whether people anticipate it. (2) c35: rain is this brief's own feature and `motion.mjs` cannot see a raindrop — drops are screen-space and absent from `__entities()`. One line there plus a screen-space exemption from the world-bounds test buys you a gate that actually covers what you changed.
